chunks: Endurance (patience) from it has four branches:

upon eagerness, fear, abstention (from the world), and anticipation (of death): So, whoever is eager for Paradise will ignore the passions; whoever fears the Fire will refrain from prohibited acts; whoever abstains from the world takes hardships lightly; and whoever anticipates death will hasten towards good deeds.

key_terms.الزُّهْدُ: Abstention or detachment from the world

ai.seo_question: What are the four aspects of patience in Shia Islamic ethics?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) categorizes patience into four distinct spiritual faculties that govern the believer's relationship with the divine and the material world, a framework deeply rooted in Shia ethical theology. This classification illustrates how internal psychological states—such as longing (shawq) and awe (shafaq)—directly manifest as disciplined external actions, forming a comprehensive roadmap for moral self-purification (tazkiyah).

en.sayed-ali-raza: eagerness, fear, abstention (from the world) and anticipation (of death). So, whoever is eager for Paradise will ignore the passions; whoever fears the Fire (of Hell) will refrain from prohibited acts; whoever abstains from the world takes hardships lightly; and whoever anticipates death will hasten towards good deeds.
